results.summary_before: This project is a digital spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) learning controller with a programmable LUT, configurable learning rate, reward-gated updates, anti-Hebbian mode, and an eligibility trace. It captures pre- and post-synaptic spike timestamps, computes weight changes, and outputs update signals. Configuration is done via SPI, and it requires external spike sources and an optional reward signal. The design is notable for its biologically inspired features and comprehensive test suite.
results.summary: This project is a digital spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) learning controller with a programmable LUT, configurable learning rate, reward-gated updates, anti-Hebbian mode, and an eligibility trace. It captures pre- and post-synaptic spike timestamps, computes weight changes, and outputs update signals. Configuration is done via SPI, and it requires external spike sources and an optional reward signal. A cocotb test suite covers reset, SPI register access, LUT programming, reward gating, anti-Hebbian inversion, and eligibility-trace decay.

results.summary_before: Flappy VGA is a simplified Flappy Bird-style game implemented entirely in digital logic, generating VGA timing and rendering a bird, moving pipes, ground, and background in real time. A physics module applies gravity and responds to a jump button, while collision detection ends the game when the bird hits a pipe or the ground. The design outputs 2-bit RGB with HSYNC and VSYNC and requires a Tiny VGA PMOD or resistor-DAC circuit plus a VGA monitor and two push buttons. It is notable for implementing a complete interactive game with sprite rendering and collision logic in a small tile area.

results.summary_before: This project implements a finite state machine that controls an automatic garage door opener, handling open, close, and stop commands from a single button plus position and obstruction sensors. Outputs drive an up motor and a down motor, and an obstruction input causes the door to stop and reverse while closing. Testing can be done with two LEDs on the motor outputs or with an H-bridge and DC motor, and the design is a straightforward educational FSM example. The documentation is clear but brief, and the design is small and self-contained.

results.summary_before: This project implements a finite state machine for a swarm microrobot drug delivery system, handling clot detection, communication, drug release, and motor control. It uses two inputs for local clot detection and nearby robot signals, and outputs drug release commands, transmission signals, and motor enables. The FSM has four states and includes a drug-available register that is cleared after release. No external hardware is required for the core logic, and the design is documented with a detailed test procedure.

results.summary_before: This project implements a configurable analog clock generation unit with a voltage-controlled MUX selecting between 3, 5, and 7-stage ring oscillators on the Sky130 process. The selection is based on a DC voltage applied to an analog input, with eight 200mV thresholds across the 0-1.8V range. Additional test structures include frequency dividers, a capacitor-loaded oscillator, and a resistor-ladder voltage reference. Testing requires a lab DC power supply and oscilloscope, and the design is notable for its analog configurability and inclusion of characterization structures.
